title: Narrow the order status
prompt: Cartwheel orders have exactly five statuses: `processing`, `shipped`, `delivered`, `cancelled` and `returned`. Replace `string` in `OrderStatus` with a union of those five literals so the type tests pass. Once the type is narrow, the compiler points at a gap in `statusLabels`: fill it so `statusLabel('returned')` returns `'Returned'`.
hints: A union of string literals looks like `'a' | 'b' | 'c'`.
After you change `OrderStatus`, read the new error on `statusLabels`: `Record<OrderStatus, string>` now requires one key per status.
explanation: With `OrderStatus` as `string`, `Record<OrderStatus, string>` means "any string keys", so a missing status is invisible and the typo `'canceled'` is a valid argument. As a union of five literals, the record must have exactly those five keys, and `canCancel('canceled')` is rejected, which is what the `@ts-expect-error` line asserts. Nothing changed at runtime except the added label: the types alone found both problems.

checks.types: The file type-checks with zero errors (including the type tests)
checks.can-cancel: `canCancel` still allows only `processing` orders to be cancelled
